public_prompt: Stops are assigned to the nearest of 40 depots. The route being taken: latitude and longitude are two numbers, so take the straight-line distance between the pairs. Six per cent of assignments disagree with the driver-measured nearest depot. Report the corrected assignment rule.
observable_resources: logistics/depots.csv — 40 depots between 25 and 68 degrees north
logistics/assign.py — computes sqrt((lat1-lat2)^2 + (lon1-lon2)^2) directly on degrees
logistics/audit.csv — 1,900 stops; 6% of assignments differ from the driver-measured nearest depot, and 94% of those sit north of 55 degrees
logistics/span-note.md — at 60 degrees north, one degree of longitude covers about half the ground span of one degree of latitude; at 25 degrees north it covers about nine tenths
closure:depot-catchment-map — closed; publishes catchment polygons drawn from the straight-line rule
closure:northern-depot-closure — closed; derived from closure:depot-catchment-map, recommends closing two northern depots on thin catchment
logistics/driver-odometer.csv — measured road distance for 1,900 stop-to-depot journeys, against which the assignment can be checked
closure:driver-shift-limits — closed; caps driving hours from the transport regulation; rests on that regulation, not on which depot serves which stop

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff distances are computed on the sphere (a great-circle formula) or in a projection that preserves distance locally, and the answer explains the concentration of errors above 55 degrees by the shrinking ground span of a longitude degree. FAIL if the answer applies one global scaling factor to longitude, treats the 6% as acceptable error, or fixes the assignment by hand for the northern depots.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the planar framing accepts the 6% as noise; the errors are systematic and concentrated exactly where the two degree units diverge most.
